title: fix(service-storage): reclaim an upload-link file no record took, through the sys_file ttl
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoAeJD7KJ2LnkshKXv2YBH8q)_

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Part of #33125 (ruling A, record 6868819455: only upload-link files that named no record and that no record took; the console remainder waits for its own card).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：agent 用"先传文件、后建记录"的上传链接传上来的文件，如果最后没有任何记录用它，30 天后由平台现有的清理流程自动删掉（数据行和文件本体一起删）。
- 为什么改：agent 或用户传完就放弃时，这些文件以前永远留在存储里，没人能看到也没人会清。
- 风险与回滚：只碰这次改动之后、经上传链接传上来且没有被任何记录认领的文件；有记录或附件引用的、以前传的、控制台传的都不动；文件引用迁移未验证的部署也只保留不删。回滚即还原本 PR，已打上的删除时间戳会留在数据里但无害。
- 先看：`attachment-lifecycle.ts` 里回收守卫新增的那一段，以及 `record-file-access.ts` 上传时打的时间戳。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run src/pre-record-upload-reclaim.integration.test.ts`，12 个用例在两种存储模式下全绿（JSON 模式下跳过 1 个）；第一个用例在 main 上会红。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **The upload marks the file.** `filesForNewRecordThroughLink` (`record-file-access.ts`) now commits each file of an upload link that named no record with `deleted_at` set to the upload time. That puts the file on the `sys_file` lifecycle's existing ttl (`deleted_at`, 30 days). No setting, sweeper or schedule is added.
- **The record that takes the file clears the mark.** In `file-reference-lifecycle.ts`, the before-write pass (`applyCopyOnClaim`) clears `deleted_at` on every marked file the write names before the driver writes, and `claimFile` clears it again when it stamps `ref_*`. A refused write leaves the file unmarked, so the file is kept and never lost.
- **The sweep checks before it deletes.** A new arm of the `sys_file` reap guard (`attachment-lifecycle.ts`) handles a committed row that carries `deleted_at`. It reclaims the row and its bytes only when all of these hold:
  - no record (`ref_*`) or attachment row holds the file,
  - no record ever held it (`released_ref_*` is empty),
  - it carries a readable upload-link binding,
  - the binding's one-hour claim window has passed,
  - the deployment's file-as-reference migration is verified (the existing `collectionOpen` gate).

  When a holder shows up, when there is no binding or a damaged one, or when the file was released, the guard clears the mark and keeps the file. While the claim window is still open, or the gate is closed, the guard keeps the file and leaves the mark. If the byte delete fails, the row stays and the guard retries on the next sweep.
- **Two checks right before the bytes go** (seat review r1):
  - **The row is read again.** The sweep judges rows from a page it read before any guard ran, so a write may have claimed the file since. The guard reads the `sys_file` row again by id and makes the whole judgment over on what it says now. If the row is no longer marked, it is kept untouched. If a holder appeared, the mark is cleared and the file kept.
  - **The bound field is asked.** A record of the bound object whose bound field holds the id keeps the file and clears the mark, even when no claim recorded it, for example after a driver-level write or a claim that failed after the field was written. A single-value field is asked by equality and a `multiple` one by `$contains`, which the SQL driver answers on the stored JSON array. When the object no longer declares the field, nothing can name the file through it, so the check passes.
  - **Where the field cannot be asked.** On SQL, a single-value file field that is still stored as JSON (a deployment that has not run the ADR-0104 column move) refuses both operators with `INVALID_FILTER`. There, `ref_*` and attachments decide alone, as they did before this check, and the sweep logs one line saying so. Any other failure of that read vetoes the row, which is retried on the next sweep.
- `sys_file.deleted_at` now describes this second use, and the en bundle is regenerated (one line).
- The tenant-audit census is recounted (`node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, plus the six hand-written prose figures on its page). The two new stamp clears are elevated `sys_file` writes, so the census now reads 313 write call sites where it read 311.
- **What is not touched:**
  - Files uploaded before this release carry no `deleted_at`, so the ttl never nominates them (ruling 「10950 不考虑存量」).
  - Console uploads are never marked.
  - Tombstoned files and never-completed uploads keep their existing paths.

## Tests

- New `src/pre-record-upload-reclaim.integration.test.ts` runs 12 cases twice on a real ObjectQL/sqlite stack: once with the file columns still JSON, and once with them moved (`fileColumnsMoved: true`). That is 23 runs, because case 11 is skipped where the columns are still JSON. Each run uses the real upload link PUT, the real `LifecycleService` sweep with its clock moved past the ttl, and the real reap guard. The cases are:
  1. measured reclaim: row and bytes are gone
  2. inside the ttl the file is untouched
  3. claim window still open: kept
  4. named by its file field on create: the mark is cleared and the file is kept
  5. named by an update
  6. a multi-file field of 3
  7. an attachment row written below the lifecycle: kept and the mark cleared
  8. an unmarked pre-change file is never a candidate
  9. control: a console upload is untouched
  10. gate closed: kept, then reclaimed once the gate opens
  11. a single-value bound field written through the driver, with no claim: kept and the mark cleared (columns moved only)
  12. a `multiple` bound field written through the driver, holding the id among others: `$contains` finds it, kept
- `src/attachment-lifecycle.test.ts` gains 15 guard cases:
  1. reclaim
  2. held through `ref_*`
  3. held by an attachment
  4. released
  5. no binding or a damaged one
  6. claim window open
  7. gate closed
  8. byte delete fails
  9. the page is unheld but the current row is held: kept, mark cleared
  10. the page is marked but the current row has been claimed and unmarked: kept, no write
  11. a single-value bound field holds the id: kept
  12. a `multiple` bound field holds it among others: kept
  13. the driver refuses the bound-field filter: reclaimed, logged once
  14. any other read failure: veto
  15. the bound object no longer declares the field: reclaimed
- `src/file-reference-lifecycle.test.ts` gains 4 cases:
  1. cleared by the before-write pass
  2. cleared by the claim alone
  3. a multiple field
  4. no mark, no extra write

## Verification

**Measured the leak first, on main 4c152685.** A throwaway copy of the measured case ran with no source change: the sweep was run one day past the 30-day ttl, and then the row and the bytes were read back. The probe was deleted afterwards. The output was:

```
MEASURE row past ttl+1d: {"status":"committed","ref_id":null,"deleted_at":null}
MEASURE bytes: true
```

The first version of the integration file (10 cases, one mode) ran 4 failed | 5 passed on main. The red cases were the measured case, inside the window, multi-file and gate closed: each asserts the mark or the reclaim. With the fix that version ran 10 passed.

**Ablated each negative pin.** I used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each ablation was restored, and afterwards the file's blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. B1 to B3 and A1 to A5 were run at 6bc9e8c3, and R1 to R2c at 8dff49cd. The table shows what went red.

| Ablation | Red |
|---|---|
| A1 drop the holder check | unit held by `ref_*` and held by attachment, integration attachment row (plus a cascade, see below) |
| A2 drop the released check | unit released |
| A3 drop the binding / finite `claim_until` check | unit no binding or damaged binding |
| A4 drop the claim-window wait | unit and integration claim window open |
| A5 drop the `collectionOpen` gate | unit and integration gate closed |
| B1 drop the before-write clear | unit before-write clear |
| B2 drop the `claimFile` clear | unit claim clear |
| B3 drop both clears together | integration named by field and named by an update |
| R1 judge the page row instead of a fresh read | unit, both stale-page cases |
| R2 the bound-field read never finds a record | unit single and multiple; integration single (columns moved) and multiple (both modes) |
| R2b treat `INVALID_FILTER` like any other failure | unit refused filter; integration measured and gate closed (columns still JSON) |
| R2c drop the "field no longer declared" pass | unit field no longer declared |

My first runs of A2, A3 and A5 were no-ops: the tool refused because the replacement text was a substring of the anchor, and nothing was ablated. I reran them with a new marker in the replacement, and they went red as listed.

In A1, once an attachment-held file is reaped, the real engine's referential-integrity error appears in later sweeps of the same file. That turned 3 more integration cases red, which is the expected cascade.

The unmarked pre-change file and the console control have no code arm to ablate. They hold structurally, because the ttl nominates only rows that carry `deleted_at`.

**Gates, at head aad3132f (rework r1)**. Main was merged at 67274aca, and the whole workspace was rebuilt first: `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` exit 0. `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 103 commands. I ran each with stdin closed, and all 103 exit 0. Reconciled with `--ran`: 103 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `pnpm lint` exits 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage test` exits 0 (1629 passed, 1 skipped), and so does `typecheck`, which includes `check:test-typecheck`. The round-0 head edaea222 also had all 103 gates green.

On the first sweep, `check-tenant-audit-census` was red: the two stamp clears are new elevated writes. The census and its page are recounted in this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- The uploader's own download of an unclaimed link file ends when the file is reclaimed, 30 days after upload at the earliest. Download, claim and hydration still key on `status`, so the mark does not change any read before that.
- The guard compares the claim window against `Date.now()`, while the ttl uses the sweep clock. In production they are the same clock. The integration tests back-date `claim_until` because only the sweep clock is advanced there.
- The gate-closed log line now reads "released, or uploaded through a link no record took" where it said "released".
- A file referenced only by a storage URL in a url field or a setting is outside scope A. The seat filed that finding separately. The console remainder (default-scope and attachments-scope uploads no record took) is a separate card, filed by the seat.
- On a SQL deployment that has not run the ADR-0104 column move, a single-value bound field cannot be asked (see What changes). There, a record that names the file through a write no claim recorded is not seen by the bound-field check, and `ref_*` decides as it did before r1. The sweep logs one line naming the remedy, `os migrate files-to-references --apply`. A `multiple` field is asked in both modes.
- No retention floor is registered for the `sys_file` ttl. A floor of the one-hour claim window would also bind the ttl of tombstoned files, which is a change outside this scope. The fresh re-read covers the race a ttl override shorter than one hour opens.
- No metadata-protocol surface and no setting changes. Only the `sys_file.deleted_at` description changes.
